correctness.rationale: Uniform radial polar integration differentiates at \(p=2\) to the exact \(q\log q\) marginal expression. Strong convexity of \(h(q)=q\log q\), with \(h''(q)=1/q\ge1\), gives a global first-order gap \(D(a)/8\). Convergence in \(C^2\) of normalized exponent deficits near signed diagonals, justified by uniform logarithmic integrability of coordinate forms, gives the strict local Hessian \(-I/(n-1)\) and limiting deficit ratio \(n/[8(n-1)]\). Compactness away from diagonal normals yields the all-normal coefficient \(1/16\) on a dimension-dependent exponent interval. The endpoint cases \(n=2\) and \(q_i=0\) are included. All 2,066 deterministic numerical checks passed, but do not substitute for the proof.

originality.rationale: König explicitly posed strictness of the derivative at the Euclidean exponent as a missing step. The proven entropy expression provides the strictness, the nondegenerate diagonal Hessian, and a uniform near-exponent global maximizing conclusion that is not implied by known subquadratic, large-exponent, or infinite-dimensional-limit results. Statement-level comparisons were made with the relevant accessible primary sources and indexed records; unindexed equivalences remain possible.
